## Lines, side by side

Line charts are the commonest 2024 type: the value axis is on the right, lines are heavy, and series are named beside the lines, with no key.

```{r g24-lines-setup}
## Lines are 1.5pt at the guide's 7pt axis labels, as measured on `20240330_CNC083`; zero lines and index rules
## are as heavy as the theme's black baseline.
g24l_line <- g24_lw(1.5)
g24l_rule <- 0.1 * g24_size / ggplot2::.pt
g24l_ink <- econ$print$text
g24l_note <- econ$print$source
g24l_ground <- econ$print$bg$value[1]
g24l_grid <- econ$print$grid

## Ticks at the year boundaries, with each label centered in its year (`20240330_CNC083`, `20240622_WBC139`): the
## boundary ticks are minor ticks drawn full length, and the labels' own ticks are hidden.
g24l_span_axis <- guide_axis(
  minor.ticks = TRUE,
  theme = theme(
    axis.ticks.x.bottom = element_line(colour = "transparent"),
    axis.minor.ticks.x.bottom = element_line(colour = g24l_ink),
    axis.minor.ticks.length.x.bottom = rel(1)
  )
)

## Labels set on the chart, at the axis-label size.
g24l_labels <- function(data, colour = g24l_ink, ...) {
  geom_text(
    data = data, aes(.data$x, .data$y, label = .data$label, hjust = .data$hjust, fontface = .data$face),
    colour = colour, size = g24_text, lineheight = 0.95, inherit.aes = FALSE, ...
  )
}
g24l_lab <- function(x, y, label, hjust = 0, face = "plain") {
  data.frame(x = x, y = y, label = label, hjust = hjust, face = face)
}
```

One series takes the single-series red; the note goes above the source.

```{r g24-lines-penumbral, econ_height = 165}
g24l_shadow <- data.frame(
  year = 2006 + 0.125 * (0:42),
  units = c(
    0.4, 0.39, 0.38, 0.39, 0.42, 0.43, 0.46, 0.5, 0.54, 0.55, 0.59, 0.65, 0.71, 0.79, 0.88, 0.98, 1.09, 1.14, 1.19,
    1.24, 1.3, 1.35, 1.39, 1.47, 1.55, 1.56, 1.54, 1.6, 1.64, 1.75, 1.88, 1.96, 2.02, 1.99, 1.95, 1.91, 1.86, 1.87,
    1.9, 1.86, 1.79, 1.73, 1.68
  )
)

g24l_penumbral <- ggplot(g24l_shadow, aes(year, units)) +
  geom_line(colour = single24[["print"]], linewidth = g24l_line) +
  g24_value_axis(
    limits = c(0, 2.05), breaks = seq(0, 2, 0.5), labels = c("0", "0.5", "1.0", "1.5", "2.0"), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(2006, 2012.05), expand = c(0, 0), guide = g24l_span_axis,
    breaks = 2006:2011 + 0.5, minor_breaks = 2006:2012, labels = c("2006", "07", "08", "09", "10", "11")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Penumbral",
    subtitle = "US shadow housing inventory*\nUnits, m",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = "*Foreclosed and delinquent homes\nnot yet on the market\nSource: CoreLogic"
  ) +
  g24_theme()

g24_chart(g24l_penumbral)
```

Two lines are red and salmon, or red and gray if the second is a reference (`20250315_FNC140`).

An index chart marks its base with a black rule and dot; a yardstick series is gray.

```{r g24-lines-transports, econ_height = 165}

g24l_car <- c(100, 99.3, 96.7, 96.6, 95.5, 94.5, 92.8, 90.8, 91.1, 89.9, 88, 87.1, 86.5, 87.3, NA)

g24l_modes <- c("Bus", "Tube", "Car", "Population")
g24l_london <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2001:2015, 4),
  mode = factor(rep(g24l_modes, each = 15), levels = g24l_modes),

)
g24l_london <- g24l_london[!is.na(g24l_london$index), ]

g24l_transports <- ggplot(g24l_london, aes(year, index, colour = mode)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 100, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  geom_line(linewidth = g24l_line, show.legend = FALSE) +
  annotate("point", x = 2001, y = 100, colour = "black", size = 2.2) +
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(c(2008.2, 2010.9, 2013, 2013.35), c(167.6, 132.5, 93.3, 107.2), g24l_modes, hjust = 0.5)) +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(80, 180), breaks = seq(80, 180, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(1999.55, 2018.2), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(2001, 2015, 2), minor_breaks = 2001:2015,
    labels = c("2001", "03", "05", "07", "09", "11", "13", "15"), guide = guide_axis(minor.ticks = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    Bus = p24[["red"]], Tube = p24[["salmon"]], Car = p24[["blue"]], Population = p24[["dark gray"]]
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Transports of delight",
    subtitle = "London’s population and journeys\n2001=100",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Sources: Transport for London; ONS;\nThe Economist"
  ) +
  g24_theme()

g24_chart(g24l_transports)
```

The palette stops at six colors; ordered categories may take a ramp (see [Ordered categories](#ordered-categories)), and the focus line is red (`20240427_ASC408`).

### Standard color order

The order is fixed: red, salmon, blue, light blue, dark gray, light gray (`economist_2024_pal()`); a single line takes the brighter single-series red.

```{r g24-lines-line-order, econ_size = "three_column", econ_height = 300}

g24l_line_shape <- list(
  A = c(
    3.62, 3.59, 3.52, 3.51, 3.48, 3.46, 3.44, 3.4, 3.34, 3.34, 3.27, 3.15, 3.09, 3.07, 3.06, 2.97,
    2.93, 2.89, 2.83, 2.8, 2.78, 2.73, 2.68, 2.68

    2.48, 2.39, 2.32, 2.23, 2.13, 2.05, 1.98, 1.97
  ),
  C = c(
    2.11, 2.11, 2.08, 1.97, 1.95, 1.96, 1.92, 1.84, 1.77, 1.68, 1.65, 1.62, 1.59, 1.49, 1.46, 1.41,
    1.37, 1.35, 1.31, 1.28, 1.25, 1.25, 1.23, 1.23
  ),

    1.89, 1.72, 1.66, 1.64, 1.62, 1.6, 1.57, 1.48
  ),

    0.23, 0.27, 0.31, 0.38, 0.46, 0.51, 0.54, 0.56, 0.56
  ),
  F = c(
    2.06, 1.98, 1.98, 1.97, 1.96, 1.98, 2.01, 2.01, 2.01, 2.04, 2.03, 2.02, 2.01, 2.01, 2.02, 2.03,
    2.02, 1.96, 1.9, 1.86, 1.85, 1.85, 1.86, 1.85
  )
)
## Which shape each series (in color order) takes in the 1- to 6-line panels.
g24l_line_panels <- list(
  c("B"),
  c("A", "B"),
  c("A", "B", "D"),
  c("A", "C", "B", "D"),
  c("A", "B", "F", "E", "D"),
  c("A", "B", "F", "D", "C", "E")
)
g24l_line_demo <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(g24l_line_panels), function(n) {
  ## One line takes the single-series red; more take the qualitative order.
  cols <- economist_2024_pal("print")(n)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(g24l_line_panels[[n]]), function(k) {
    data.frame(
      panel = paste(n, if (n == 1) "line" else "lines"),
      series = paste(n, k),
      colour = cols[k],
      x = 1:24,
      y = g24l_line_shape[[g24l_line_panels[[n]][k]]]
    )
  }))
}))
g24l_line_demo$panel <- factor(g24l_line_demo$panel, levels = unique(g24l_line_demo$panel))

g24_chart(
  ggplot(g24l_line_demo, aes(x, y, group = series, colour = colour)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = g24_lw(2)) +
    facet_wrap(~panel, nrow = 2) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.8, 25.6), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.76, 4.69), breaks = 0:4, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    labs(title = "Standard colour order", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    g24_theme() +
    g24_no_axes() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = g24l_grid))
)
```

### Highlighting a line against a background

The rest go light gray, named together once; the focus line is the emphasis red, on top and a little heavier, with a bold black name.

Two focus series take red and blue; a label lost in the gray takes a short black leader.

```{r g24-lines-pricier, econ_height = 185}
## Approximate values read to follow the chart, smoothed to monthly.
g24l_rent_at <- c(
```

### Markers and rank charts

Where observations are few or uneven, mark each with an unoutlined dot in the line's own color (`20250301_DAC769`); a truncated axis takes the broken-scale mark (see [Broken scales](#broken-scales)).

A rank chart puts an order in place of a value, rank 1 at the top (`20240720_CNC447`).

```{r g24-lines-rank-setup}
## Measured on `20240720_CNC447`: the rest are a warm light gray, not the palette's `#C6C8CA`; the dark gray is the
## palette's. The line is about 1.8pt and the markers about 3.3pt across, at the guide's 7pt axis labels.
g24l_rank_gray <- "#BABAAD"
g24l_rank_line <- g24_lw(1.8)
g24l_rank_dot <- g24_lw(3.3)
```

```{r g24-lines-rank, econ_height = 215}
## Read from the chart: the rank of each reason in each survey, from first to tenth (`NA` where it was not ranked).
g24l_rank_year <- c(2004, 2009, 2014, 2023)
g24l_rank_data <- list(
  `Connections` = c(3, 4, 3, 1), `Grew up in a rich family` = c(NA, 6, 5, 2), `Better opportunities` = c(5, 5, 4, 3),
  `Ability and talent` = c(1, 1, 1, 4), `Hard work` = c(4, 2, 2, 5), `Unfair economic\nsystem` = c(7, 9, 9, 6),
  `High education` = c(2, 3, 6, 7), `Parents with high\neducation level` = c(NA, 8, 8, 8),
  `Good luck` = c(6, 7, 7, 9), `Dishonesty` = c(8, 10, 10, 10)
)
g24l_ranks <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(g24l_rank_data), function(n) {
  data.frame(reason = n, year = g24l_rank_year, rank = g24l_rank_data[[n]])
}))
## Drawn from the back: the grays first, then the colors, the red last.
g24l_rank_cols <- c(
  `Connections` = p24[["red"]], `Ability and talent` = p24[["blue"]], `High education` = p24[["light blue"]],
  `Grew up in a rich family` = p24[["salmon"]], `Unfair economic\nsystem` = p24[["dark gray"]]
)
g24l_rank_cols <- c(
  stats::setNames(rep(g24l_rank_gray, 5), setdiff(names(g24l_rank_data), names(g24l_rank_cols))),
  g24l_rank_cols[c("Unfair economic\nsystem", "High education", "Grew up in a rich family", "Ability and talent",
                   "Connections")]
)
g24l_ranks$reason <- factor(g24l_ranks$reason, levels = names(g24l_rank_cols))
g24l_ranks <- g24l_ranks[order(g24l_ranks$reason), ]
g24l_rank_end <- g24l_ranks[g24l_ranks$year == 2023, ]

g24l_rank_plot <- ggplot(g24l_ranks, aes(year, rank, group = reason, colour = reason)) +
  ## The gridlines and the baseline run from the first survey to the last, and no further.
  geom_gridline_economist_2024(1:10, 2004, 2023, base_size = g24_size) +
  annotate("segment", x = 2004, xend = 2023, y = 10.38, yend = 10.38, colour = g24l_ink,
           linewidth = 0.1 * g24_size / ggplot2::.pt) +
  ## Two reasons were not ranked in 2004: their lines start in 2009.
  geom_line(linewidth = g24l_rank_line, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_point(size = g24l_rank_dot, stroke = 0, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ## The names stand beside the last survey, level with their points, in black.
  geom_text(data = g24l_rank_end, aes(2024.3, rank, label = reason), colour = "black", hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5,
            lineheight = 0.95, size = g24_text, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g24l_rank_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_reverse(limits = c(10.38, 0.8), breaks = 1:10, expand = c(0, 0),
                  labels = c("1st", "2nd", "3rd", paste0(4:10, "th"))) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(2004, 2042.5), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(2004, 2009, 2014, 2023),
                     ## An en space pads "2004" and "09", so that the labels of surveys five years apart do not meet.
                     labels = c("2004\u2002", "\u200209", "14", "23")) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "It’s who you know", subtitle = "China, reasons given for why\npeople are rich, rank*",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: Big Data China,\nCSIS and Stanford"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = rel(17 / 15)),
    axis.ticks.length.x = unit(0.8 * g24_size, "pt")
  )

g24_chart(g24l_rank_plot, footnote = "*Based on surveys", number = 1)
```

#### A white ground with a short red tab

A white ground with a short red tab is the print layout on white, not a web graphic (`20250301_DAC769`).
### Smoothed lines through points

Where the data are noisy, a heavy fitted line carries the trend over small translucent dots in the series' color; parties take their [party colors](#party-colors).

```{r g24-lines-smooth-setup}
## The dots: each series' own color, translucent, smaller than the line is wide.
g24l_dot_fade <- 0.45
g24l_poll_dot <- 0.9

## A loess fit through each series' points, over that series' own span.
g24l_loess <- function(points, span = 0.5, n = 100) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(points, points$series, drop = TRUE), function(d) {
    fit <- stats::loess(y ~ x, d, span = span)
    x <- seq(min(d$x), max(d$x), length.out = n)
    data.frame(series = d$series[1], x = x, y = stats::predict(fit, data.frame(x = x)))
  }))
}

## Noisy points around a trend: the trend through `at` and `value`, sampled at `x`, plus normal noise.
g24l_noisy <- function(series, x, at, value, sd) {
  data.frame(series = series, x = x, y = stats::approx(at, value, xout = x, rule = 2)$y + stats::rnorm(length(x), 0, sd))
}
```

```{r g24-lines-smooth-catch, econ_height = 185}
## Invented polls around trends read to follow the chart: one poll a week, months as decimals from 1 January.
set.seed(2024)
g24l_poll_x <- seq(1.1, 7.7, by = 0.23)
g24l_catch_points <- rbind(
  g24l_noisy("Trump", g24l_poll_x, c(1, 2, 2.2, 3.2, 4, 5, 6, 7.7), c(-8.5, -5.5, -5.2, -13.5, -13.5, -14, -14, -12),
             sd = 1.8),
  g24l_noisy("Biden", g24l_poll_x, c(1, 2, 3.2, 4, 5, 6, 7.7), c(-13, -10.3, -17, -18.8, -18, -19, -21.8), sd = 2),
  g24l_noisy("Harris", g24l_poll_x, c(1, 2, 3.2, 3.8, 4.4, 5, 6, 7.7), c(-13, -10.5, -15.5, -18, -16.3, -16.7, -17.2,
             -15.5), sd = 2)
)
g24l_catch_cols <- c(Trump = single24[["print"]], Harris = p24[["blue"]], Biden = econ$print$sequential_gray$value[3])
g24l_catch_lines <- g24l_loess(g24l_catch_points, span = 0.5)
## Harris, the subject, is drawn last, on top.
g24l_order <- function(d) {
  d$series <- factor(d$series, levels = c("Biden", "Trump", "Harris"))
  d[order(d$series), ]
}

g24l_catch <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x, y, colour = series, group = series)) +
  geom_point(data = g24l_order(g24l_catch_points), size = g24l_poll_dot, alpha = g24l_dot_fade, stroke = 0) +
  geom_line(data = g24l_order(g24l_catch_lines), linewidth = g24l_line) +
  ## Harris's name sits clear of the lines, below them, with a curved leader up to hers.
  annotate("curve", x = 3.25, xend = 4.35, y = -21.6, yend = -16.9, curvature = 0.35, colour = g24l_ink,
           linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(c(3.75, 1.35, 6.05), c(-8.6, -21.6, -22.6), c("Donald Trump", "Kamala Harris", "Joe Biden")),
              vjust = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g24l_catch_cols, guide = "none") +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(-26, 0.3), breaks = seq(-25, 0, 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(1, 8.3), expand = c(0, 0), guide = g24l_span_axis,
    breaks = 1:7 + 0.5, minor_breaks = 1:8, labels = month.abb[1:7]
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Catch him if you can",
    subtitle = "United States, net favourability\nrating*, 2024, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = "*Favourable minus unfavourable\nSource: YouGov/The Economist"
  ) +
  g24_theme()

g24_chart(g24l_catch)
```

Events are thin dark gray rules, named once in gray.

```{r g24-lines-smooth-switching, econ_height = 185}
## Invented survey waves around trends read to follow the chart: three waves a year.
set.seed(2015)
g24l_wave_x <- seq(2014.15, 2023.4, by = 1 / 3)
g24l_wave_at <- c(2014, 2015.4, 2016.2, 2017.4, 2018.2, 2019.2, 2020.2, 2021.2, 2022.2, 2023.4)
g24l_switch_points <- rbind(
  g24l_noisy("Labour/Green", g24l_wave_x, g24l_wave_at, c(8.5, 12.8, 14, 18.3, 17.2, 16.6, 18, 18.6, 20, 22.4), sd = 1.2),
  g24l_noisy("Labour/Lib Dem", g24l_wave_x, g24l_wave_at, c(9.8, 13, 15, 17.5, 17.6, 18.6, 19, 19.5, 19.8, 20),

  g24l_noisy("Lib Dem/Green", g24l_wave_x, g24l_wave_at, c(6.2, 8.5, 10, 12.5, 15, 16, 15, 14.4, 15, 16.8), sd = 1.2),
  g24l_noisy("Labour/Conservative", g24l_wave_x, g24l_wave_at, c(6.6, 7.6, 7.2, 8.5, 6.8, 4.8, 6.6, 7, 6.6, 5.8),

)
```

In panels, first and second terms take red and salmon or blue and light blue.

```{r g24-lines-smooth-tanking, econ_height = 330}
## Invented polls around trends read to follow the chart. The first panel counts days from each inauguration; the
## second, days from 1 January of each first year in office.
set.seed(2025)
g24l_terms <- c("Obama", "Biden", "Trump I", "Trump II")
g24l_tank_panels <- c("President", "President’s handling of the economy")
g24l_tank_points <- rbind(
  cbind(panel = g24l_tank_panels[1], rbind(
    g24l_noisy("Obama", seq(0, 500, 8), c(0, 80, 150, 220, 280, 360, 430, 500), c(37, 20, 18, 7, 8, 0, 0, -2), sd = 3),
    g24l_noisy("Biden", seq(0, 500, 8), c(0, 60, 100, 180, 240, 300, 360, 420, 500), c(15, 10, 12, 8, -5, -6, -10, -9,
               -8), sd = 3),
    g24l_noisy("Trump I", seq(0, 500, 8), c(0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500), c(-3, -8, -14, -14, -12, -10), sd = 2.5),
    g24l_noisy("Trump II", seq(0, 84, 8), c(0, 50, 85), c(3, 1, -10), sd = 2.5)
  )),
  cbind(panel = g24l_tank_panels[2], rbind(
    g24l_noisy("Biden", seq(20, 120, 9), c(20, 45, 75, 95, 120), c(10.5, 11, 8, 7, 10), sd = 2),
    g24l_noisy("Trump I", seq(20, 115, 9), c(20, 41, 60, 80, 115), c(11, 3.5, 7.5, 2.5, 4.5), sd = 2),
    g24l_noisy("Trump II", seq(20, 100, 7), c(20, 41, 56, 70, 85, 100), c(11, 3, 1, -3, -4.5, -8), sd = 2)
  ))
)
g24l_tank_points$panel <- factor(g24l_tank_points$panel, levels = g24l_tank_panels)
g24l_tank_lines <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(g24l_tank_points, g24l_tank_points$panel), function(d) {
  cbind(panel = d$panel[1], g24l_loess(d, span = 0.55))
}))
g24l_tank_cols <- c(Obama = p24[["light blue"]], Biden = p24[["blue"]], `Trump I` = p24[["salmon"]],
                    `Trump II` = p24[["red"]])
g24l_tank_lab <- function(panel, x, y, label, face = "plain") {
  cbind(panel = factor(g24l_tank_panels[panel], levels = g24l_tank_panels), g24l_lab(x, y, label, face = face))
}

g24l_tanking <- ggplot(mapping = aes(x, y, colour = series, group = series)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  geom_point(data = g24l_tank_points, size = g24l_poll_dot, alpha = g24l_dot_fade, stroke = 0) +
  geom_line(data = g24l_tank_lines, linewidth = g24l_line) +
  g24l_labels(rbind(
    g24l_tank_lab(1, c(310, 75, 82, 330), c(10.5, 5.5, -2.8, -17.5), c("Obama", "Biden", "Trump II", "Trump I"),
                  face = c("plain", "plain", "bold", "plain")),
    g24l_tank_lab(2, c(96, 90, 42), c(12.6, 1.4, -5.5), c("Biden", "Trump I", "Trump II"),
                  face = c("plain", "plain", "bold"))
  ), vjust = 0.5) +
  ## The first panel's axis title, under its numbers; the second panel's months need none.
  g24l_labels(g24l_tank_lab(1, 250, -33, "Days after inauguration"), hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free", axes = "all") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g24l_tank_cols, guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  ## The panels share scales by range: days 0-500 in the first, and January to April in the second.
  g24_value_axis(
    limits = function(l) if (l[2] > 25) c(-21, 41) else c(-11, 15.4),
    breaks = function(l) if (l[2] > 25) seq(-20, 40, 20) else seq(-10, 15, 5),
    expand = c(0, 0), oob = scales::oob_keep
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = function(l) if (l[2] > 200) c(-8, 520) else c(15, 125), expand = c(0, 0),
    breaks = function(l) if (l[2] > 200) seq(0, 500, 100) else c(16, 45.5, 75, 105.5),
    ## The first panel's ticks sit at its numbers; minor breaks on the majors would be dropped, so they are nudged.
    minor_breaks = function(l) if (l[2] > 200) seq(0, 500, 100) + 0.01 else c(1, 32, 60, 91, 121),
    labels = function(b) if (max(b, na.rm = TRUE) > 200) b else month.abb[1:4][seq_along(b)],
    guide = g24l_span_axis
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Tanking",
    subtitle = "United States, net approval,\npercentage points",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Sources: YouGov/The Economist; The Economist"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(margin = margin(3.5, 0, 9, 0)),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(3.2 * g24_size, "pt")
  )

g24_chart(g24l_tanking)
```

### Confidence ribbons

A band of uncertainty is a translucent ribbon in the series' own color under the heavy line (`20250329_EPC233`), with no name and no key and a faint hairline edge so that overlaps show (`geom_ribbon_economist_2024()`).
A gridline stops short of a name standing on it (`geom_gridline_economist_2024()`).

```{r g24-lines-poll-position, econ_height = 215}
## Invented to follow the chart: weekly poll averages from the 2021 election to 25 March 2025, as decimal years, each
## series a few knots joined by a smooth curve, with a little week-to-week noise, and a 95% interval around it.
set.seed(2025)
g24l_wk <- seq(2021.72, 2025.23, length.out = 175)
g24l_knots <- function(x, y, hw, noise = 0.3) {
  ## The interval's half-width: one number, or a few spread evenly over the span.
  hw <- if (length(hw) == 1) rep(hw, length(g24l_wk)) else
    stats::approx(seq(0, 1, length.out = length(hw)), hw, xout = (g24l_wk - min(g24l_wk)) / diff(range(g24l_wk)))$y
  jitter <- as.numeric(stats::filter(stats::rnorm(length(g24l_wk), 0, noise), 0.5, method = "recursive"))
  mid <- stats::spline(x, y, xout = g24l_wk, method = "natural")$y + jitter
  ## The ribbons stop at the top of the panel, as the Liberal one does in the original.
  data.frame(x = g24l_wk, y = mid, lo = pmax(mid - hw, 0), hi = pmin(mid + hw, 50.9))
}
g24l_polls <- rbind(
  cbind(series = "Conservative", g24l_knots(
    c(2021.72, 2021.85, 2022, 2022.3, 2022.7, 2022.95, 2023.2, 2023.6, 2024, 2024.5, 2024.8, 2024.93, 2025.05, 2025.23),
    c(33.5, 29, 29.5, 33, 34, 33.3, 38, 40, 41.5, 43, 44.5, 43, 38, 36.8), hw = 5, noise = 0.35)),
  cbind(series = "Liberal", g24l_knots(
    c(2021.72, 2022, 2022.5, 2023, 2023.5, 2023.9, 2024.3, 2024.8, 2024.95, 2025.05, 2025.15, 2025.23),
    c(33, 32, 30.5, 28.5, 28, 24.5, 23.5, 21.5, 19.5, 25, 36, 43), hw = c(4, 4.5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 6, 9, 11, 11),
    noise = 0.35)),
  cbind(series = "New Democratic", g24l_knots(
    c(2021.72, 2021.9, 2022.4, 2022.8, 2023.2, 2023.9, 2024.4, 2024.8, 2024.95, 2025.1, 2025.23),
    c(18, 19.8, 19.7, 18.7, 20, 18, 18.5, 19, 16.5, 14, 8.7), hw = 3, noise = 0.3)),
  cbind(series = "Bloc Québécois", g24l_knots(
    c(2021.72, 2021.9, 2022.5, 2023.2, 2023.9, 2024.5, 2024.85, 2025.1, 2025.23),
    c(7.5, 6.5, 7.1, 6.9, 7.2, 8.2, 8.5, 6.8, 5.7), hw = 2, noise = 0.12)),
  cbind(series = "People’s Party", g24l_knots(
    c(2021.72, 2021.9, 2022, 2022.3, 2022.6, 2023, 2024, 2024.8, 2025.23),
    c(4.8, 6, 6.2, 4.3, 3.3, 2.8, 2.2, 1.9, 1.7), hw = c(2.5, 2.5, 2, 2, 1.5), noise = 0.12)),
  cbind(series = "Green", g24l_knots(
    c(2021.72, 2021.85, 2022.4, 2022.8, 2023.2, 2023.6, 2024.3, 2024.6, 2024.95, 2025.23),
    c(2.7, 3.9, 3.6, 4.2, 3.5, 4.8, 4.4, 4.1, 3.8, 1.7), hw = 1.5, noise = 0.12))
)
g24l_poll_names <- c("Conservative", "Liberal", "New Democratic", "Bloc Québécois", "People’s Party", "Green")
g24l_polls$series <- factor(g24l_polls$series, levels = g24l_poll_names)
## The party colors: the palette's red, blue and light blue, and the amber, dark red and green of the party table.
g24l_poll_cols <- c(
  Conservative = p24[["blue"]], Liberal = p24[["red"]], `New Democratic` = "#FCB315", `Bloc Québécois` = p24[["light blue"]],
  `People’s Party` = "#B7131A", Green = "#71BF45"
)

## Gridlines are drawn by hand (`geom_gridline_economist_2024()`), broken where a name stands on them.
g24l_poll_gaps <- data.frame(y = c(50, 30, 10), from = c(2023.95, 2024.35, 2023.75), to = c(2025, 2024.93, 2024.95))

g24l_poll_position <- ggplot(mapping = aes(colour = series)) +
  geom_gridline_economist_2024(seq(10, 50, 10), 2021.72, 2025.23, g24l_poll_gaps, base_size = g24_size) +
  geom_ribbon_economist_2024(aes(x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = series, group = series), data = g24l_polls) +
  geom_line(data = g24l_polls, aes(x, y, group = series), linewidth = g24l_line) +
  ## The name of the People's Party has no room beside its line: a black leader runs down to it.
  annotate("segment", x = 2022.23, xend = 2022.23, y = 9.6, yend = 4.4, colour = g24l_ink, linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(c(2024, 2024.37, 2021.88, 2023.78, 2021.88, 2021.88), c(50.4, 30.4, 14.4, 10.4, 10.8, 1.3),
                       c("Conservative", "Liberal", "New Democratic", "Bloc Québécois", "People’s Party", "Green")),
              vjust = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g24l_poll_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = g24l_poll_cols, guide = "none") +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 51), breaks = seq(0, 50, 10), expand = c(0, 0), oob = scales::oob_keep) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(2021.72, 2025.23), expand = c(0, 0), guide = g24l_span_axis, oob = scales::oob_keep,
    breaks = c(2021.86, 2022.5, 2023.5, 2024.5, 2025.115), minor_breaks = c(2021.72, 2022:2025, 2025.23),
    labels = c("2021", "22", "23", "24", "25*")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "In poll position", subtitle = "Canada, voting intention in\ngeneral election, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: National polls"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

g24_chart(g24l_poll_position, footnote = "*To March 25th")
```

Solid ribbons suit two or three series: an opaque, unedged tint of each line, named once, "Confidence interval", by a curved leader.

```{r g24-lines-industrial-decline, econ_height = 215}
## Read from the chart: annual estimates, 1982 to March 2025, and the half-width of each confidence interval.
g24l_wage <- data.frame(
  year = rep(1982:2025, 2),
  series = rep(c("All", "No college"), each = 44),
  value = c(
    11.2, 10.5, 10.8, 12.0, 11.9, 11.3, 10.5, 10.2, 10.1, 9.9, 10.1, 10.0, 9.7, 9.7, 9.3, 8.9, 8.5, 8.2, 7.4, 7.9,
    7.3, 5.5, 4.7, 4.6, 4.4, 5.0, 5.0, 5.5, 5.4, 5.8, 5.8, 5.8, 5.7, 6.4, 5.0, 5.8, 5.6, 6.0, 5.6, 6.0, 6.3, 5.1,
    5.1, 2.8,
    8.0, 7.5, 8.0, 9.8, 9.5, 8.3, 8.3, 8.1, 8.1, 8.1, 7.8, 7.3, 8.0, 6.6, 6.0, 5.5, 5.8, 5.5, 4.4, 4.6, 4.5, 1.6,
    0.9, 0.8, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.8, 0.9, 1.4, 1.4, 1.4, 1.5, 2.4, -1.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.8, 0.6, 1.0, 1.7, 1.0, 1.3, -0.3
  ),
  hw = c(rep(0.7, 41), 1.0, 1.2, 2.3, rep(0.8, 33), rep(1.2, 8), 1.5, 1.8, 3.0)

## Solid tints, not translucent ones: the gray line and its light gray, the red line and its pale salmon.
g24l_wage_line <- c(All = "#77787B", `No college` = p24[["red"]])
g24l_wage_band <- c(All = "#CACAC6", `No college` = "#F1CAB4")

g24l_industrial <- ggplot(g24l_wage, aes(year, value, group = series)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = value - hw, ymax = value + hw, fill = series)) +
  ## The gridlines go over the ribbons, so they are drawn as a layer; the zero rule is black.
  geom_gridline_economist_2024(c(5, 10, 15), 1979.8, 2029.9, base_size = g24_size) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = series), linewidth = g24l_line) +
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(c(1988.7, 1988.7), c(13.2, 2.3), c("All", "No college")), vjust = 0.5) +
  ## The ribbons are named once, with a leader ending in a dot on the red one.
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(2004.7, -2.6, "Confidence interval", hjust = 1), colour = g24l_note, vjust = 0.5) +
  annotate("curve", x = 2005.2, y = -2.6, xend = 2008.1, yend = -0.8, curvature = 0.5, colour = g24l_note,
           linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  annotate("point", x = 2008.1, y = -0.8, colour = g24l_note, size = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g24l_wage_line, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = g24l_wage_band, guide = "none") +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(-5.2, 15.3), breaks = seq(-5, 15, 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(1979.8, 2029.9), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = c(1982, seq(1985, 2025, 5)),
    labels = c("1982", "", "90", "95", "2000", "05", "10", "15", "20", "25†")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Industrial decline",
    subtitle = "United States, manufacturing workers’ wage\npenalty or premium*, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "*Controlling for age, education, ethnicity, gender,\nmarriage status and more   †To March\n",
      "Sources: Economic Policy Institute,\nCurrent Population Survey Extracts; The Economist"
    )
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

g24_chart(g24l_industrial)
```

### Forecasts on lines

A forecast continues the line in the same color, dotted, with a gray "Forecast" key at the top left (`20240720_BRC433`).
```{r g24-lines-prison-breaks, econ_height = 175}
## Approximate values read to follow the chart. The solid stretches end where the data end, in early 2024; the dotted
## ones start there.
g24l_prison_anchor <- function(at, value, from, to, by = 1 / 12) {
  data.frame(year = seq(from, to, by), value = approx(at, value, seq(from, to, by))$y)
}
g24l_cap <- g24l_prison_anchor(
  c(2011, 2011.2, 2011.5, 2012, 2012.5, 2012.7, 2012.9, 2013.2, 2013.4, 2014, 2014.5, 2015, 2015.2, 2015.6, 2016,
    2016.5, 2017, 2017.5, 2018, 2018.5, 2019, 2019.5, 2019.9, 2020, 2020.1, 2020.5, 2021, 2021.5, 2022, 2022.5, 2023,
    2023.5, 2024, 2024.3),
  c(88.2, 87, 87.6, 88.8, 90, 89, 87, 86.8, 85, 85.5, 86, 86.2, 85, 86.5, 86.8, 86, 85.6, 86.5, 85.8, 85, 84.5, 84.8,
    85, 83, 81.5, 81, 80.5, 81, 82, 84, 87, 88.8, 89, 88.5),
  2011, 2024.3
)
g24l_pop <- g24l_prison_anchor(
  c(2011, 2011.3, 2011.5, 2012, 2012.5, 2012.8, 2013.2, 2013.5, 2014, 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2018.7, 2019, 2019.5,
    2019.9, 2020, 2020.1, 2020.5, 2021, 2021.5, 2022, 2022.5, 2023, 2023.5, 2023.8, 2024.2),
  c(84.5, 85, 87, 86.5, 86.8, 83.2, 83, 84.5, 84.5, 84.8, 85, 84.5, 84.8, 83.5, 83, 84, 84.7, 82, 79.5, 79, 78.2,
    79.5, 80.5, 82.5, 85, 88, 87.2, 87.2),
  2011, 2024.2
)
g24l_cap_fc <- g24l_prison_anchor(c(2024.3, 2025, 2026, 2027, 2028), c(88.8, 91, 93.3, 95.5, 98), 2024.3, 2028)
g24l_pop_fc <- g24l_prison_anchor(
  c(2024.2, 2024.6, 2025, 2025.65, 2026.7, 2027.5, 2028), c(87.8, 92, 97, 101.4, 103.5, 104.7, 105.5), 2024.2, 2028
)

## The dotted stretch is a linetype of the same width: equal dots and gaps, a little longer than the line is wide.
g24l_forecast_lty <- "21"
## The key's sample is a gray a step lighter than the text gray (sampled in `20240720_BRC433`, about #969796).
g24l_key_gray <- econ$print$sequential_gray$value[3]

g24l_prison_breaks <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(year, value), g24l_cap, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_line) +
  geom_line(aes(year, value), g24l_pop, colour = p24[["red"]], linewidth = g24l_line) +
  geom_line(aes(year, value), g24l_cap_fc, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_line, linetype = g24l_forecast_lty) +
  geom_line(aes(year, value), g24l_pop_fc, colour = p24[["red"]], linewidth = g24l_line, linetype = g24l_forecast_lty) +
  ## The key: a dotted gray sample and its name, at the top left of the panel.
  annotate(
    "segment", x = 2011.05, xend = 2012.55, y = 105, yend = 105, colour = g24l_key_gray, linewidth = g24l_line,
    linetype = g24l_forecast_lty
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 2012.9, y = 105, label = "Forecast", hjust = 0, size = g24_text, colour = g24l_ink) +
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(2011, 95.5, "Operational capacity")) +
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(2024.6, 107.8, "Population", hjust = 0.5), colour = p24[["red"]]) +
  geom_scale_break_economist_2017() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(65, 111), breaks = seq(70, 110, 10), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(2011, 2028.1), expand = c(0, 0), guide = g24l_span_axis,
    breaks = c(seq(2011, 2025, 2) + 0.5, 2028), minor_breaks = 2011:2028,
    labels = c("2011", "13", "15", "17", "19", "21", "23", "25", "28")
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Prison breaks",
    subtitle = "England and Wales, prison population\nand capacity, ’000",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Sources: Ministry of Justice; Institute for Government"
  ) +
  g24_theme()

g24_chart(g24l_prison_breaks)
```

#### A forecast with a range

A projection with a range puts a salmon fan behind a solid red line, named "Range" with a curved arrow (`20241019_FNC437`).

```{r g24-lines-debt-president, econ_height = 190}
## Read from the chart `20241019_FNC437`: the official projection from 2023, the plans' central projection and its
## range from 2025, when the two part.
g24l_cbo <- data.frame(year = 2023:2035, value = c(97, 99, 102, 104, 106, 109, 111, 113, 115, 117, 120, 122, 125))
g24l_plans <- data.frame(
  year = 2025:2035,
  value = c(102, 105, 110, 114, 118, 122, 124, 129, 133, 138, 142),
  lo = 102 + 2.6 * (0:10),
  hi = 102 + 5.8 * (0:10)
)
## The fan: the salmon, about half opaque, so that the gridlines show through.
g24l_fan_alpha <- 0.5
## The comparison line's warm gray.
g24l_cbo_gray <- "#A4A495"

g24l_debt_president <- ggplot(mapping = aes(year, value)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), data = g24l_plans, fill = p24[["salmon"]], alpha = g24l_fan_alpha) +
  geom_line(data = g24l_cbo, colour = g24l_cbo_gray, linewidth = g24l_line) +
  geom_line(data = g24l_plans, colour = p24[["red"]], linewidth = g24l_line) +
  ## The range is named once, with a curved arrow into the fan.
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(2032.4, 149.7, "Range", hjust = 1), colour = g24l_note, vjust = 0.5) +
  annotate(
    "curve", x = 2032.6, y = 150, xend = 2033.1, yend = 143.5, curvature = -0.6, colour = g24l_note,
    linewidth = g24l_rule, arrow = arrow(length = unit(2.5, "pt"), angle = 35)
  ) +
  g24l_labels(g24l_lab(2028.2, 98.8, "Current Congressional\nBudget Office projections"), colour = g24l_note,
              vjust = 0.5) +
  ## The baseline stops at the last year; the gridlines run on under the value labels, beyond the fan.
  annotate("segment", x = 2022.2, xend = 2035, y = 74, yend = 74, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  geom_scale_break_economist_2017() +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(74, 160.5), breaks = seq(80, 160, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(2022.2, 2037), expand = c(0, 0), breaks = seq(2023, 2035, 2),
    labels = economist_2017_year_format()
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Debt president",
    subtitle = "United States, projected debt based\non Donald Trump’s plans, % of GDP",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  theme(axis.line.x = element_blank())

g24_chart(g24l_debt_president)
```

Which forecast convention to use:

* **Dotted lines** for a line that carries on from its data, keyed "Forecast" (`20240720_BRC433`).
* **A salmon fan** behind a solid red line for a range of outcomes (`20241019_FNC437`).
* **A shaded block** the height of the panel behind areas and bars, named "Forecast" in gray at its top (`20240921_WBC092`; see [Lines, stacked](#lines-stacked)).
* **A shaded band** behind dots (`20250906_WBC303`; see [Scatter over time, with a forecast band](#scatter-over-time-with-a-forecast-band)).

## Lines, stacked

Stacked areas stack from the baseline up in palette order, red at the bottom, with thin white rules between bands, which are named inside in regular type; bands too thin to name go in a key above the plot.

```{r g24-lines-foreign-hoards, econ_height = 154}
g24l_china <- c(0.26, 0.36, 0.56, 0.77, 1.02, 1.49, 1.91, 2.3, 2.64, 2.96)
g24l_other <- c(0.77, 0.98, 1.23, 1.51, 2.03, 2.86, 3.02, 3.19, 3.54, 3.77)
g24l_reserves <- data.frame(
  year = rep(2002:2011, 2),
  trn = c(g24l_china, g24l_other),
  region = factor(
    rep(c("China", "Other developing countries"), each = 10),
    levels = c("China", "Other developing countries")
  )
)

## A white rule along the top of every band but the last, and the forecast years under a darker block, as in
## `20240921_WBC092`.
g24l_hoards <- ggplot(g24l_reserves, aes(year, trn, fill = region, colour = region)) +
  geom_area(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), outline.type = "upper", linewidth = g24_lw(0.75)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2009, xmax = 2011, ymin = 0, ymax = 6.8, fill = p24[["dark gray"]], alpha = 0.18) +
  annotate("text", x = 2010, y = 6.3, label = "Forecast", vjust = 1, size = g24_text, colour = g24l_note) +
  annotate("text", x = 2008.6, y = 1.3, label = "China", hjust = 1, colour = "white", size = g24_text) +
  annotate(
    "text", x = 2006.4, y = 3.85, label = "Other\ndeveloping\ncountries", hjust = 1, size = g24_text,
    lineheight = 0.95
  ) +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 6.8), breaks = seq(0, 6, 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(2001.52, 2012), breaks = c(2002, 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2011),
    labels = c("2002", "04", "06", "08", "10", "11")
  ) +
  scale_fill_economist_2024("print", guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("white", NA), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = "Foreign hoards",
    subtitle = "Developing-country currency reserves\n$trn",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: IMF"
  ) +
  g24_theme()

g24_chart(g24l_hoards)
```

```{r g24-lines-big-shift, econ_height = 178}
    6, 5.4, 5.4, 5.3, 5.6, 6.9, 5.4, 7.2, 7.7, 6.3, 5.6, 7.4, 6.9, 4.9, 4.9, 4.9, 7, 6, 4, 6.3, 8.8, 7.9, 6.7, 5.8,
    4.7, 4.4, 5.3, 5.3, 4.6, 4.4, 4.6, 4.9
  )
)
g24l_havens <- names(g24l_shift_bands)
g24l_shift <- do.call(rbind, lapply(g24l_havens, function(haven) {
  data.frame(year = 1982:2013, haven = factor(haven, levels = g24l_havens), pct = g24l_shift_bands[[haven]])
}))

## The widest band is named in place; the five thinner ones go in the key, in stack order.
g24l_big_shift <- ggplot(g24l_shift, aes(year, pct, fill = haven, colour = haven)) +
  geom_area(position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), outline.type = "upper", linewidth = g24_lw(0.75)) +
  annotate("text", x = 2012.5, y = 7.5, label = "Netherlands", hjust = 1, colour = "white", size = g24_text) +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 60.6), breaks = seq(0, 60, 10), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(1980.2, 2016.5), breaks = c(1982, 1985, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005, 2010, 2013),
    labels = c("1982", "", "90", "95", "2000", "05", "10", "13")
  ) +
  scale_fill_economist_2024("print", breaks = g24l_havens[-1]) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(rep("white", 5), NA), guide = "none") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  labs(
    title = "The big shift",
    subtitle = "Tax havens’ share of US overseas\ncorporate profits, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Source: “The Hidden Wealth of Nations”,\n",
      "by Gabriel Zucman, University of Chicago\nPress, 2015"
    )
  ) +
  g24_theme()

g24_chart(g24l_big_shift)
```

A stack can carry its total as a dark gray line along the top, and a series outside the stack runs over it as an ordinary red line (`20250201_USC522`).


When one ordered category is the story, it takes red and the rest a ramp through salmon into grays (see the [color section](#ordered-categories)); the focus band is named in bold.

## Thermometer

The dot range is the 2017 thermometer: a solid dot per series, a dark gray rule from the lowest dot to the highest, the scale on top with a black zero rule, and a key of dots above the plot (`20240706_AMC263`).

```{r g24-lines-thermometer-data}
g24l_fields <- c(
  "Mathematics", "Economics", "Computer Science", "Business", "Biology",
  "Philosophy", "English", "Psychology", "History", "Communication"
)
g24l_series_names <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six")

## One table of values per series count.
g24l_thermo_values <- list(
  `2` = list(
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33),
    c(416, 398, 382, 316, 308, 275, 290, 239, 283, 251)
  ),
  `3` = list(
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33),
    c(418, 398, 382, 316, 308, 275, 290, 239, 283, 251),
    c(395, 316, 292, 266, 257, 215, 201, 199, 197, 187)
  ),
  `4` = list(
    c(280, 249, 117, 191, 84, 148, 80, 60, 134, 121),
    c(402, 316, 292, 266, 257, 214, 201, 199, 197, 187),
    c(339, 397, 381, 315, 307, 275, 290, 239, 283, 250),
    c(31, 40, 72, 36, 39, 43, 35, 15, 20, 33)
  ),
  `6` = list(
    c(222, 191, 172, 133, 16, 180, 152, 104, 233, 109),
    c(405, 398, 382, 316, 308, 276, 290, 238, 284, 251),
    c(280, 249, 117, 192, 84, 147, 80, 60, 135, 121),
    c(31, 40, 72, 37, 39, 43, 35, 15, 21, 34),
    c(335, 294, 134, 236, 129, 196, 52, 199, 260, 156),
    c(375, 317, 292, 266, 257, 214, 201, 199, 197, 187)
  ),
  dot = list(
    c(31, 41, 72, 37, 39, 43, 35, 15, 21, 34),
    c(419, 398, 382, 280, 308, 276, 290, 239, 284, 251),
    c(396, 317, 364, 263, 257, 215, 201, 222, 197, 187)
  )
)

g24l_thermo_data <- function(key) {
  values <- g24l_thermo_values[[key]]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(values), function(k) {
    data.frame(
      field = factor(g24l_fields, levels = rev(g24l_fields)),
      series = factor(g24l_series_names[k], levels = g24l_series_names),
      value = values[[k]]
    )
  }))
}

## The dark gray rule runs from the lowest dot to the highest; the dots are drawn over it in series order.
g24l_thermo_plot <- function(key, colours = unname(p24)) {
  d <- g24l_thermo_data(key)
  spans <- merge(
    stats::aggregate(value ~ field, d, min),
    stats::aggregate(value ~ field, d, max),
    by = "field", suffixes = c("_lo", "_hi")
  )
  label_gp <- gpar(fontsize = g24_size, fontface = "bold", fontfamily = economist_2017_font(), col = g24l_ink)
  ggplot(d, aes(y = .data$field)) +
    geom_segment(
      data = spans, aes(x = .data$value_lo, xend = .data$value_hi, y = .data$field, yend = .data$field),
      colour = p24[["dark gray"]], linewidth = g24_lw(1)
    ) +
    geom_point(aes(x = .data$value, colour = .data$series), size = 1.75) +
    ## "Horrible" sits on the axis-number row, over the category labels.
    annotation_custom(textGrob(
      "“Horrible”", gp = label_gp, hjust = 0, vjust = 0,
      x = unit(0, "npc") - grobWidth(textGrob("Computer Science", gp = gpar(fontsize = g24_size))) -
        unit(0.3 * g24_size, "pt"),
      y = unit(1, "npc") + unit(0.25 * g24_size, "pt")
    )) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    scale_x_continuous(position = "top", limits = c(0, 425), breaks = seq(0, 400, 100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 1.75))) +
    labs(
      title = "The horrible science",
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Use of specific “adjective” per million\n",
        "words in student reviews on\n",
        "RateMyProfessors.com*"
      ),
      x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL, caption = "Source: Ben Schmidt, Northeastern University"
    ) +
    g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
    theme(
      ## Gridlines run both ways: a horizontal one through each category, under its rule and dots.
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = g24l_grid),
      axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0)
    )
}
```

### Standard color order

Series take the qualitative order: red, salmon, blue, light blue; more than four is "probably too many".

```{r g24-lines-thermometer-2, econ_height = 185}
g24_chart(g24l_thermo_plot("2"))
```

```{r g24-lines-thermometer-3, econ_height = 185}
g24_chart(g24l_thermo_plot("3"))
```

```{r g24-lines-thermometer-4, econ_height = 185}
g24_chart(g24l_thermo_plot("4"))
```

```{r g24-lines-thermometer-6, econ_height = 185}
g24_chart(g24l_thermo_plot("6"))
```

### Dot terminals

Dots are the terminal, not rules; dated series run gray, salmon, red, oldest to newest (`20240706_AMC263`).
Web charts add arrows for a change between two dates (see [below](#arrows-and-lollipops)).

```{r g24-lines-thermometer-dots, econ_height = 185}
## The oldest dot in the warm gray of `20240706_AMC263`, the second step of the gray ramp.
g24_chart(g24l_thermo_plot("dot", colours = c(econ$print$sequential_gray$value[3], p24[["salmon"]], p24[["red"]])))
```

### Arrows and lollipops

A change between two dates is a dark gray arrow from a salmon dot to a red one ("Gills and spills"), with a key of dots above the plot.

```{r g24-lines-thermometer-arrows, econ_height = 200}
g24l_parties <- c("Labour", "Conservative", "Reform†", "Liberal Democrat", "Other")
g24l_gills <- data.frame(
  party = factor(g24l_parties, levels = rev(g24l_parties)),
  then = c(28.5, 61.5, 0, 5.5, 5.5),
  now = c(55, 23, 14.5, 5.5, 2.5)
)
## Arrows only where the dots do not touch; each stops at the edge of its dots.
g24l_gap <- 2.9
g24l_moves <- g24l_gills[abs(g24l_gills$now - g24l_gills$then) > 2 * g24l_gap, ]
g24l_moves$dir <- sign(g24l_moves$now - g24l_moves$then)
g24l_dates <- c("Current voting intention*", "2019")
g24l_gills_dots <- data.frame(
  party = rep(g24l_gills$party, 2),
  value = c(g24l_gills$then, g24l_gills$now),
  when = factor(rep(rev(g24l_dates), each = nrow(g24l_gills)), levels = g24l_dates)
)

g24l_gills_plot <- ggplot(g24l_gills_dots, aes(value, party)) +
  geom_segment(
    data = g24l_moves,
    aes(x = .data$then + .data$dir * g24l_gap, xend = .data$now - .data$dir * g24l_gap, y = .data$party,
      yend = .data$party),
    colour = p24[["dark gray"]], linewidth = g24_lw(1.5), linejoin = "mitre",
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.5 * g24_size, "pt"), angle = 30, type = "closed")
  ) +
  ## The 2019 dots first, so the current ones lie on top.
  geom_point(aes(colour = .data$when), data = g24l_gills_dots[order(g24l_gills_dots$when, decreasing = TRUE), ],
    size = 2.6) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", limits = c(0, 80), breaks = seq(0, 80, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  ## The arrows' layer holds only the parties that moved, so the rows are named in order here.
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(g24l_parties)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(p24[["red"]], p24[["salmon"]])) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2.2))) +
  labs(
    title = "Gills and spills",
    subtitle = "Gillingham and Rainham constituency,\ngeneral-election vote share, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "*Face-to-face constituency poll of 376 people,\nJune 4th-16th 2024\n†Brexit Party in 2019\n",
      "Sources: House of Commons Library; WeThink;\nThe Economist"
    )
  ) +
  g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = g24l_grid),
    axis.line.y = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )

g24_chart(g24l_gills_plot)
```

An arrow can stand without dots ("Electric car prices"): a heavy single-series red stroke, the dates named once at the ends of one arrow.

```{r g24-lines-arrows, econ_height = 120}
## A heavy arrow: a thick shaft that stops inside a head drawn with a hairline, since a closed head drawn with the
## shaft's own line width is swollen by its stroke. `back` is how far into the head the shaft stops, in data units.
g24l_heavy_arrow <- function(data, back, shaft = 3.5) {
  data$dir <- sign(data$to - data$from)
  list(
    geom_segment(
      aes(x = .data$from, xend = .data$to - .data$dir * back, y = .data$y, yend = .data$y, colour = I(.data$col)),
      data = data, linewidth = g24_lw(shaft), lineend = "butt", inherit.aes = FALSE
    ),
    geom_segment(
      aes(x = .data$to - .data$dir * back, xend = .data$to, y = .data$y, yend = .data$y, colour = I(.data$col)),
      data = data, linewidth = g24_lw(0.3), linejoin = "mitre", inherit.aes = FALSE,
      arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.8 * shaft, "pt"), angle = 34, type = "closed")
    )
  )
}

g24l_ev <- data.frame(
  country = factor(c("US", "Britain", "China"), levels = c("China", "Britain", "US")),
  from = c(181, 171, 116),
  to = c(158, 145, 85)
)

g24l_ev_plot <- ggplot(g24l_ev, aes(y = country)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 100, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  g24l_heavy_arrow(transform(g24l_ev, y = country, col = single24[["print"]]), back = 3) +
  ## The dates, once, at the ends of Britain's arrow, on the ground so the gridline breaks around them.
  geom_label(
    data = data.frame(x = c(128, 187), y = "Britain", label = c("2022", "2018")),
    aes(x = .data$x, y = .data$y, label = .data$label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = g24_text, colour = g24l_ink, fill = g24l_ground, linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(1, "pt")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", limits = c(70, 205), breaks = seq(75, 200, 25), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title = "Electric car prices",
    subtitle = "As % of non-electric cars, pre-subsidies",
    x = NULL, y = NULL, caption = "Source: International Energy Agency"
  ) +
  g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = g24l_grid),
    axis.line.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0),
    ## The small web charts set the headline in red, with no tab, over a subtitle in regular weight.
    plot.title = element_text(colour = accent24[["print"]]),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "plain")
  )

g24_chart(g24l_ev_plot, tab = c(0, 0))
```

Where arrows run both ways, color them by direction in red and blue.

```{r g24-lines-arrows-two-way, econ_height = 205}
g24l_g7_names <- c("Canada", "Britain", "Germany", "France", "Japan", "Italy", "United States")
g24l_trust <- data.frame(
  country = factor(g24l_g7_names, levels = rev(g24l_g7_names)),
  from = c(57, 62.5, 55, 54, 48, 41, 63),
  to = c(65, 64, 62, 61, 60, 55, 48)
)
g24l_trust$dir <- ifelse(g24l_trust$to > g24l_trust$from, "rise", "fall")

g24l_key_gp <- gpar(fontsize = g24_size, fontfamily = economist_2017_font(), col = g24l_ink)
## The key starts at the left edge of the chart, where the category names do.
g24l_key_left <- unit(0, "npc") - grobWidth(textGrob("United States", gp = gpar(fontsize = g24_size,
  fontface = "bold"))) - unit(0.3 * g24_size, "pt")
g24l_key_y <- unit(1, "npc") + unit(2.4 * g24_size, "pt")
g24l_two_way_key <- gTree(children = gList(
  textGrob("2006", x = g24l_key_left, y = g24l_key_y, hjust = 0, gp = g24l_key_gp),
  segmentsGrob(
    x0 = g24l_key_left + unit(3.2 * g24_size, "pt"), x1 = g24l_key_left + unit(5.6 * g24_size, "pt") - unit(3, "pt"),
    y0 = g24l_key_y, y1 = g24l_key_y,
    gp = gpar(col = econ$print$sequential_gray$value[3], lwd = 3.5 / 0.75, lineend = "butt")
  ),
  segmentsGrob(
    x0 = g24l_key_left + unit(5.6 * g24_size, "pt") - unit(3, "pt"), x1 = g24l_key_left + unit(5.6 * g24_size, "pt"),
    y0 = g24l_key_y, y1 = g24l_key_y, arrow = arrow(length = unit(6.3, "pt"), angle = 34, type = "closed"),
    gp = gpar(col = econ$print$sequential_gray$value[3], fill = econ$print$sequential_gray$value[3], lwd = 0.4)
  ),
  textGrob("2023", x = g24l_key_left + unit(6, "pt") * g24_size, y = g24l_key_y, hjust = 0, gp = g24l_key_gp)
))
## The break mark: a short zigzag on the axis-number row, before the first number.
g24l_axis_break <- polylineGrob(
  x = unit(c(0, 0.3, 0.45, 0.6, 0.75, 1), "npc"),
  y = unit(1, "npc") + unit(0.75 * g24_size, "pt") + unit(c(0, 0, 2, -2, 0, 0), "pt"),
  gp = gpar(col = g24l_ink, lwd = 0.8)
)

g24l_outlier <- ggplot(g24l_trust, aes(y = country)) +
  g24l_heavy_arrow(
    transform(g24l_trust, y = country, col = ifelse(dir == "rise", p24[["blue"]], p24[["red"]])), back = 0.8
  ) +
  annotation_custom(g24l_two_way_key) +
  annotation_custom(g24l_axis_break, xmin = 35.6, xmax = 38.2) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(position = "top", limits = c(35, 72), breaks = seq(40, 70, 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = g24_bold_label("United States")) +
  labs(
    title = "Outlier",
    subtitle = "G7 countries, confidence in\nnational institutions*, %",
    x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "*Key national institutions: the military, the judicial\n",
      "system, the national government and the honesty\nof elections\nSource: Gallup"
    )
  ) +
  g24_theme(horizontal = FALSE) +
  theme(
    axis.line.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = 4 * g24_size))
  )

g24_chart(g24l_outlier)
```

### Log scales on a lollipop

A lollipop on a log scale ("No brakes", `20240608_WBC240`) labels the 1-2-5 sequence as major gridlines, with lighter minor lines for the other values and "Log scale" ending the subtitle.

```{r g24-lines-brakes-data}
## Approximate values read to follow the chart: log10 of the multiple at 502px per log10(20) from 100x at x=46 in
## `20240608_WBC240` (608px wide).
g24l_brakes <- data.frame(
  ceo = c("Hock Tan, Broadcom", "William Lansing, Fair Isaac", "Tim Cook, Apple", "Hamid Moghadam, Prologis",
          "Ted Sarandos, Netflix", "David Zaslav, Warner Bros. Discovery", "Glenn Fogel, Booking Holdings",
          "Shantanu Narayen, Adobe", "Neil Hunn, Roper Technologies", "Bill McDermott, ServiceNow"),
  px = c(222, 370, 379, 416, 419, 420, 429, 436, 451, 466)
)
g24l_brakes$multiple <- 100 * 20^((g24l_brakes$px - 46) / 502)
g24l_brakes$row <- rev(seq_len(nrow(g24l_brakes)))
## The minor lines, other than 1-2-5 values; they start at the second row's line.
g24l_minor <- c(300, 400, 600, 700, 800, 900)
```

```{r g24-lines-brakes, econ_height = 265}
g24l_brakes_plot <- ggplot(g24l_brakes, aes(multiple, row)) +

  geom_text(aes(x = 106, y = row + 0.38, label = ceo), hjust = 0, size = g24_text) +
```

## Scatter plot

Gridlines run both ways, with black zero rules where zero is in range; the value-axis title is ranged right above the axis and the x-axis title centered under it.

```{r g24-lines-scatter-setup}
## The value-axis title, ranged right above the axis, and the room it needs under the subtitle.
## On a log x axis, pass the panel's x limits: the default bounds, -Inf and Inf, have no logarithm.
g24l_y_title <- function(label, xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf) {
  annotation_custom(textGrob(
    label, x = unit(1, "npc"), y = unit(1, "npc") + unit(1.5 * g24_size, "pt"), hjust = 1, vjust = 0,
    gp = gpar(fontsize = g24_size, fontfamily = economist_2017_font(), col = g24l_ink, lineheight = 0.95)
  ), xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax)
}
g24l_scatter_theme <- function(title_lines = 1) {
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = g24l_grid),
    axis.line.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = g24_size * (1.9 + 1.2 * title_lines)))
  )
}
## Standard dots: the single-series red, translucent and unoutlined. Highlight dots: the emphasis red, opaque, in a
## thin black outline. Both sampled from `20260829_BRC066`.
g24l_dot_alpha <- 0.6
g24l_dot_size <- 1.3
g24l_outline <- 0.35
```

### Chart elements

A standard dot is the single-series red at about 60% opacity, unoutlined; a highlight dot is the emphasis red, opaque, with a thin black outline and a name; a trend line is dashed, in red.
Category dots take palette colors, translucent (`20260117_WOC860`).

```{r g24-lines-scatter-elements, econ_size = "one_column", econ_height = 410}
## The specimen is laid out in points from its bottom left; the dots are drawn larger than life.
g24l_spec_row <- c(320, 220, 120, 40)
g24l_spec_dots <- data.frame(
  x = rep(c(14, 23, 32), 3),
  y = rep(g24l_spec_row[1:3], each = 3) + rep(c(0, 4, -3), 3),
  size = c(rep(5, 6), 3, 5, 6.5),
  fill = c(
    rep(alpha(single24[["print"]], g24l_dot_alpha), 3), rep(p24[["red"]], 3),
    alpha(p24[["blue"]], g24l_dot_alpha), alpha(p24[["salmon"]], g24l_dot_alpha),
    alpha(p24[["dark gray"]], g24l_dot_alpha)
  ),
  colour = c(rep("transparent", 3), rep("black", 3), rep("transparent", 3))
)
g24l_spec_notes <- data.frame(
  x = 52,
  y = c(
    g24l_spec_row[1] + c(18, 6, -6, -18, -30),
    g24l_spec_row[2] + c(18, 6, -6, -18, -30),
    g24l_spec_row[3] + c(18, 6, -6, -18, -30),
    g24l_spec_row[4] + c(18, 6, -6)
  ),
  label = c(
    "Standard dot", "single-series red", "60% opacity, no outline", "where the trend matters", "more than any point",
    "Highlight dot", "emphasis red, opaque", "thin black outline", "for named outliers and", "important points",
    "Category dot", "palette colors, translucent", "no outline", "for groups and bubbles;", "outline those named",
    "Trend line", "dashed, red", "lighter than a data line"
  ),
  face = c(
    "bold", rep("plain", 4), "bold", rep("plain", 4), "bold", rep("plain", 4), "bold", "plain", "plain"
  )
)

ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = g24l_spec_dots, aes(x, y, size = size, fill = fill, colour = colour), shape = 21, stroke = 0.6
  ) +
  annotate(
    "segment", x = 4, xend = 42, y = g24l_spec_row[4] + 6, yend = g24l_spec_row[4] + 6,
    colour = p24[["red"]], linewidth = g24_lw(1), linetype = "42"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = g24l_spec_notes, aes(x, y, label = label, fontface = face), hjust = 0, size = g24_text
  ) +
  scale_size_identity() +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 150), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(10, 350), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(title = "Chart elements", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  g24_theme() +
  g24_no_axes()
```

### Standard scatter

Trend lines are dashed in the house red, one per group in its color; the story's period is red, the earlier gray (`20260829_BRC066`).

```{r g24-lines-divergent, econ_height = 195}
set.seed(2017)
## The 1990-2007 cloud is tight and steep; the 2012-16 cloud is wide and flat.
## Five 1990-2007 outliers sit out to the right.
g24l_metro_old <- data.frame(employment = rnorm(240, 1.6, 1.1))
g24l_metro_old$house_prices <- 1.3 + 2.2 * g24l_metro_old$employment + rnorm(240, 0, 1.8)
g24l_metro_old <- rbind(
  g24l_metro_old,
  data.frame(employment = c(4.4, 4.8, 5.1, 5.9, 8.2), house_prices = c(2.8, 8.2, 7.9, 7.6, 6.6))
)
g24l_metro_new <- data.frame(employment = rnorm(210, 2.1, 1.6))
g24l_metro_new$house_prices <- 3.5 + 0.67 * g24l_metro_new$employment + rnorm(210, 0, 3.9)

g24l_metro_periods <- c("Q1 1990 - Q1 2007", "Q1 2012 - Q1 2016")
g24l_metro <- rbind(
  cbind(period = g24l_metro_periods[1], g24l_metro_old),
  cbind(period = g24l_metro_periods[2], g24l_metro_new)
)
g24l_metro$period <- factor(g24l_metro$period, levels = g24l_metro_periods)

## Trend lines run over the span the guide draws them.
g24l_trends <- data.frame(
  period = factor(g24l_metro_periods, levels = g24l_metro_periods),
  x = c(-1.5, -0.7), xend = c(5.8, 8.2),
  y = c(-2, 3), yend = c(14.2, 9)
)
g24l_period_cols <- c("Q1 1990 - Q1 2007" = p24[["dark gray"]], "Q1 2012 - Q1 2016" = single24[["print"]])
g24l_trend_cols <- c("Q1 1990 - Q1 2007" = p24[["dark gray"]], "Q1 2012 - Q1 2016" = p24[["red"]])

g24l_divergent <- ggplot(g24l_metro, aes(employment, house_prices)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = period), size = g24l_dot_size, alpha = g24l_dot_alpha, stroke = 0) +
  geom_segment(
    data = g24l_trends, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = g24l_trend_cols,
    linewidth = g24_lw(1), linetype = "42"
  ) +
  g24l_y_title("House prices") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.4, 8.8), ylim = c(-5, 20), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-2, 8, 2)) +
  g24_value_axis(breaks = seq(-5, 20, 5)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g24l_period_cols) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2.1, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(
    title = "Divergent",
    subtitle = "United States, housing and employment\nMetro areas*, average annual change, %",
    x = "Employment", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    caption = "*At least 100,000 population\nSources: Freddie Mac; US Bureau of Labour Statistics"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  g24l_scatter_theme() +
  ## The key sits under the subtitle, and the axis title between it and the plot.
  theme(
    plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = g24_size)),
    legend.box.spacing = unit(g24_size * 3.2, "pt")
  )

g24_chart(g24l_divergent)
```

Named points are highlight dots with black names, on leader lines where they sit away (`20260829_BRC066`).

```{r g24-lines-disinfectant, econ_height = 166}
set.seed(11)
## A diffuse cloud of countries, plus a denser band of more open, less corrupt ones.
g24l_corruption <- data.frame(open = c(runif(55, 19, 63), runif(24, 60, 92)))
g24l_corruption$score <- c(
  pmin(55, pmax(5, 0.55 * (g24l_corruption$open[1:55] - 19) + 10 + rnorm(55, 0, 13))),
  runif(24, 33, 70)
)
g24l_named <- data.frame(
  country = c("Britain", "Denmark", "India", "Colombia", "US", "Sweden", "Mexico", "Singapore"),
  open = c(77.5, 91.7, 37.8, 37, 73.8, 86.8, 34.9, 83.7),
  score = c(96.5, 82.5, 67.4, 66, 69.6, 65.6, 53, 34.4),
  ## Where each label sits, relative to its dot, in data units.
  lx = c(76, 84.5, 42.8, 34.1, 70.9, 95.2, 19.6, 83.7),
  ly = c(91, 91, 75.4, 67.4, 70.2, 50, 52.6, 26.7),
  hjust = c(1, 0, 0.5, 1, 1, 0.5, 1, 0.5)
)
## Leader lines for the two labels that sit away from their dots.
g24l_leaders <- data.frame(
  x = c(20.5, 86.8, 92.6), xend = c(34.9, 92.6, 92.6),
  y = c(53, 65.6, 65.6), yend = c(53, 65.6, 55)
)

g24l_disinfectant <- ggplot(g24l_corruption, aes(open, score)) +
  geom_point(colour = single24[["print"]], size = g24l_dot_size, alpha = g24l_dot_alpha, stroke = 0) +
  geom_segment(
    data = g24l_leaders, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = "black", linewidth = g24_lw(0.5)
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = g24l_named, shape = 21, fill = p24[["red"]], colour = "black", size = g24l_dot_size,
    stroke = g24l_outline
  ) +
  geom_text(data = g24l_named, aes(x = lx, y = ly, label = country, hjust = hjust), size = g24_text) +
  g24l_y_title("Open-data index score,\nlatest, 100=most open") +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 115), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "The best disinfectant",
    subtitle = "Corruption and open data",
    x = "Corruption-perceptions index score, 2014\n100=least corrupt", y = NULL,
    caption = "Sources: Transparency International;\nOpen Knowledge Foundation"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  g24l_scatter_theme(title_lines = 2)

g24_chart(g24l_disinfectant)
```

### Scatter over time, with a forecast band

A scatter over time has a line chart's axis; dots are opaque with a darker outline, and the forecast years are a gray block under them, named "Forecast" at its middle ("Energy bills", `20250906_WBC303`).

```{r g24-lines-energy-data}
## Invented plants, scattered to follow the chart; the named outliers are placed as drawn.
set.seed(303)
g24l_plant <- function(country, year, cost) data.frame(country = country, year = year, cost = cost)
g24l_plants <- rbind(
  ## The US: a cluster of cheap early plants, the 1980s overruns, a few later ones.
  g24l_plant("US", runif(34, 1972, 1984), 0.7 + (runif(34, 1972, 1984) - 1972) * 0.12 + abs(rnorm(34, 0, 0.5))),
  g24l_plant("US", runif(26, 1984.5, 1990), pmin(10.5, pmax(3, 4 + runif(26, 0, 5.5) + rnorm(26, 0, 1.6)))),
  g24l_plant(
    "US", c(1986.4, 1988.4, 1989.4, 1990.4, 1993.4, 1996.5, 2016.8, 2023.6, 2024.3, 1990.1),
    c(12.7, 10.3, 5.7, 7.1, 8.8, 6.5, 6.0, 15, 15, 8.8)
  ),
  ## France: a long, flat line of plants near $1.5-2.5 per W, one 2025 forecast.
  g24l_plant("France", runif(40, 1977, 1993), 1.4 + abs(rnorm(40, 0, 0.35))),
  g24l_plant("France", c(1994, 1999.8, 2000.6, 2025.1), c(2.4, 2.3, 3.0, 9.9)),
  g24l_plant(
    "South Korea",
    c(1978.5, 1983.7, 1984.2, 1985, 1986, 1987, 1988, 1989, 1990.5, 1992.4, 1996.2, 1997, 1998, 1998.8, 1999.7,
      2002, 2003.3, 2004, 2005),
    c(4.2, 4.6, 4.5, 2.8, 3.3, 3.2, 3.2, 3.2, 2.6, 2.6, 3.5, 3.5, 3.5, 2.7, 2.7, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 2.4)
  ),
  ## China: one early expensive plant, a few in the 2000s, then a dense, flat band out to the forecast.
  g24l_plant("China", c(1993.8, 1994.1, 2001.8, 2002.5, 2003.2, 2004, 2007.5), c(8.3, 2.3, 2.3, 2.1, 3.2, 3.2, 2.7)),
  g24l_plant("China", runif(70, 2010.5, 2029), 1.55 + abs(rnorm(70, 0, 0.3))),
  g24l_plant("China", c(2016, 2016.6, 2018.8, 2019.3, 2025.5, 2026.5, 2027.5), c(3.2, 3.4, 3.3, 3.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.4))
)
## Drawn in the key's order, so that the last country, China, lies on top.
g24l_plants$country <- factor(g24l_plants$country, levels = c("US", "France", "South Korea", "China"))
g24l_plants <- g24l_plants[order(g24l_plants$country), ]
## Each outline is the fill a quarter of the way to black, as sampled on `20250906_WBC303`
## (`#659BD2` fill, `#26449B` outline; `#ED1C24` fill, a dark red outline).
g24l_darker <- function(col) vapply(col, function(x) colorRampPalette(c(x, "black"))(5)[2], character(1))
g24l_plant_fill <- c(US = p24[["blue"]], France = p24[["light blue"]], `South Korea` = p24[["salmon"]],
                     China = p24[["red"]])
```

```{r g24-lines-energy, econ_height = 240}
g24l_energy <- ggplot(g24l_plants, aes(year, cost)) +
  ## The forecast: the dark gray at 15% over the ground, sampled as `#D8D7CE` on `#ECEBE0` in `20250906_WBC303`.
  annotate("rect", xmin = 2024.1, xmax = 2029, ymin = 0, ymax = 15, fill = p24[["dark gray"]], alpha = 0.15) +
  annotate("text", x = 2026.3, y = 7.4, label = "Forecast", size = g24_pt(7.5), colour = g24l_note) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = country, colour = country), shape = 21, size = 1.55, stroke = g24l_outline) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = g24l_plant_fill) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = g24l_darker(g24l_plant_fill)) +
  g24_value_axis(limits = c(0, 15), breaks = seq(0, 15, 3), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1972, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020, 2029),
    labels = c("1972", "80", "90", "2000", "10", "20", "29"), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(1969.1, 2032.4), clip = "off") +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(size = 2.1)),
    colour = "none"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Energy bills",
    subtitle = "Nuclear power plants*, construction cost†,\n$ per W, 2020 prices",
    x = "Date of commercial operation", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "*Includes retired plants\n†If construction was completed overnight\n",
      "Source: \"Can China break the 'cost curse' of\nnuclear power?\", by S. Liu, G. He, M. Qiu and\n",
      "D.M. Kammen, Nature, 2025"
    )
  ) +

    axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5),

  )

g24_chart(g24l_energy, number = 3)
```

### Highlighted dots over a background, on a log scale

Highlighted dots are opaque, ringed in black and named in black over a translucent red background ("Health over wealth", `20240706_ASC302`); the subject takes the emphasis red and a bold name.
A log x axis is labelled in powers of ten, with "log scale" ending the axis title and no minor gridlines.

```{r g24-lines-health-data}
## Positions read in pixels off `20240706_ASC302` (608px wide): log10 of GDP at 159.3px per decade from 1 at x=194,
## life expectancy at 9.94px per year from 90 at y=187.
g24l_asc_x <- function(px) 10^((px - 194) / 159.3)
g24l_asc_y <- function(py) 90 - (py - 187) / 9.94

g24l_countries <- data.frame(
  country = c("Thailand", "France", "Germany", "US", "China", "Poland", "Vietnam", "Malaysia", "India", "Indonesia",
              "Afghanistan", "Nigeria"),
  dot_x = c(333, 460, 470, 503, 370, 409, 301, 371, 259, 306, 135, 231),
  dot_y = c(288, 254, 265, 289, 299, 301, 339, 322, 367, 376, 444, 547),
  ## Where each name is set (its anchor, in pixels) and how it is ranged to that anchor.
  lab_x = c(283, 457, 461, 520, 388, 453, 276, 363, 224, 306, 84, 243),
  lab_y = c(265, 208, 318, 267, 277, 348, 306, 373, 350, 402, 465, 566),
  hjust = c(0.5, 0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.5, 0, 1, 0, 0.5, 0, 0.5, 0)
)
g24l_countries$gdp <- g24l_asc_x(g24l_countries$dot_x)
g24l_countries$life <- g24l_asc_y(g24l_countries$dot_y)
g24l_countries$name_x <- g24l_asc_x(g24l_countries$lab_x)
g24l_countries$name_y <- g24l_asc_y(g24l_countries$lab_y)
g24l_countries$subject <- g24l_countries$country == "Thailand"

## The other countries with over 20m people: approximate, read to follow the chart. A merged dot is two or three.
set.seed(302)
g24l_blobs <- data.frame(
  x = c(441, 482, 440, 436, 379, 334, 311, 279, 359, 288, 396, 377, 262, 314, 288, 214, 216, 156, 253, 204, 217, 321,
        232, 168, 186, 260, 440),
  y = c(243, 251, 272, 306, 308, 314, 315, 319, 325, 334, 335, 341, 347, 361, 368, 379, 414, 443, 449, 448, 457, 457,
        467, 479, 483, 485, 245),
  k = c(2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 3, 4, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)
)
g24l_others <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(g24l_blobs)), function(i) {
  b <- g24l_blobs[i, ]
  data.frame(px = b$x + c(0, rnorm(b$k - 1, 0, 6))[seq_len(b$k)], py = b$y + c(0, rnorm(b$k - 1, 0, 7))[seq_len(b$k)])
}))
g24l_others$gdp <- g24l_asc_x(g24l_others$px)
g24l_others$life <- g24l_asc_y(g24l_others$py)

## Leader lines, as pixel pairs: from the name to the dot.
g24l_leaders_straight <- data.frame(
  x = c(460, 470, 371), xend = c(460, 470, 371), y = c(222, 273, 330), yend = c(247, 303, 358)
)
g24l_leaders_curved <- data.frame(x = c(277, 411), xend = c(298, 452), y = c(306, 311), yend = c(332, 348))
g24l_leader_px <- function(d) {
  data.frame(x = g24l_asc_x(d$x), xend = g24l_asc_x(d$xend), y = g24l_asc_y(d$y), yend = g24l_asc_y(d$yend))
}
```

```{r g24-lines-health, econ_height = 250}
g24l_health <- ggplot(g24l_others, aes(gdp, life)) +
  geom_point(colour = single24[["print"]], size = 1.55, alpha = g24l_dot_alpha, stroke = 0) +
  geom_segment(
    data = g24l_leader_px(g24l_leaders_straight),
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = "black", linewidth = g24_lw(0.5), inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_curve(
    data = g24l_leader_px(g24l_leaders_curved[1, ]),
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = "black", linewidth = g24_lw(0.5), curvature = -0.5,
    ncp = 8, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_curve(
    data = g24l_leader_px(g24l_leaders_curved[2, ]),
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend), colour = "black", linewidth = g24_lw(0.5), curvature = 0.5,
    ncp = 8, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = g24l_countries, aes(fill = subject), shape = 21, colour = "black", size = 1.7, stroke = g24l_outline
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = g24l_countries, aes(name_x, name_y, label = country, hjust = hjust, fontface = ifelse(subject, "bold", "plain")),
    size = g24_text
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = p24[["red"]], `FALSE` = single24[["print"]]), guide = "none") +
  g24l_y_title("Life expectancy\nat birth, years", xmin = 0.1, xmax = 300) +
  g24_value_axis(breaks = seq(50, 90, 10)) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100), labels = c("0.1", "1", "10", "100"), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.1, 300), ylim = c(46.5, 90), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
  labs(
    title = "Health over wealth", subtitle = "Selected countries*, 2023†",
    x = "GDP per person, $'000, log scale", y = NULL,
    caption = "*Population greater than 20m\n†Or latest available, estimate\nSources: IMF; United Nations"
  ) +
  g24_theme() +
  g24l_scatter_theme(title_lines = 1)

g24_chart(g24l_health)
```

### Bubble chart

Bubbles are translucent, unoutlined and sized by area, with dot and nested-circle keys inside the panel (`20260117_WOC860`); direction labels are gray, in sentence case, with an arrow.

```{r g24-lines-vitality-data}
set.seed(4)
g24l_regions <- c("Northeast", "Midwest", "West", "South")
## Per region: number of counties, health score mean and spread, swing at the mean health, and
## how large the counties are (log-mean of voting-eligible population).
g24l_region_spec <- data.frame(
  region = g24l_regions, n = c(150, 700, 70, 450),
  health_mean = c(42, 37.5, 50, 47), health_sd = c(6, 5, 8, 9),
  swing_mean = c(12, 15, -2, 5), swing_sd = c(7, 9, 11, 8), size_mean = c(1.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.8)
)
g24l_counties <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(g24l_region_spec)), function(i) {
  r <- g24l_region_spec[i, ]
  health <- pmin(66, pmax(22, rnorm(r$n, r$health_mean, r$health_sd)))
  data.frame(
    region = r$region,
    health = health,
    swing = r$swing_mean - 1 * (health - r$health_mean) + rnorm(r$n, 0, r$swing_sd),
    pop = rlnorm(r$n, r$size_mean, 0.75)
  )
}))
## Drawn from the southern cloud up, so the Midwest and Northeast lie on top.
g24l_counties$region <- factor(g24l_counties$region, levels = c("South", "West", "Midwest", "Northeast"))
g24l_counties <- g24l_counties[order(g24l_counties$region), ]
g24l_counties$region <- factor(g24l_counties$region, levels = g24l_regions)

g24l_region_cols <- c(
  Northeast = p24[["red"]], Midwest = p24[["salmon"]], West = p24[["blue"]], South = p24[["light blue"]]
)
g24l_bubble_alpha <- 0.55

## The key, inside the panel at the top right: regions, then bubble size.
g24l_vitality_key <- function(show_regions = TRUE) {
  region_key <- if (show_regions) {
    list(
      annotate("text", x = 61.1, y = 46.5, label = "Region", hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = g24_text),
      annotate(
        "point", x = 61.6, y = c(40.5, 34.5, 28.5, 22.5), size = 2.1, colour = g24l_region_cols,
        alpha = g24l_bubble_alpha
      ),
      annotate("text", x = 63, y = c(40.5, 34.5, 28.5, 22.5), label = g24l_regions, hjust = 0, size = g24_text)
    )
  }
  c(region_key, list(
    annotate("point", x = 62.8, y = c(12.5, 9.4), shape = 1, size = c(6.6, 1.9), stroke = 0.3),
    annotate(
      "text", x = 65.6, y = c(16, 10.5, 5), label = c("Voting", "eligible", "population"), hjust = 0,
      size = g24_text
    )
  ))
}

## Direction labels in gray with arrows, along the zero rule and under either end of the health axis.
g24l_direction_labels <- list(
  annotate(
    "text", x = 20.6, y = c(2.5, -2.5), label = c("↑ More Republican", "↓ Less Republican"),
    hjust = 0, vjust = c(0, 1), size = g24_text, colour = g24l_note
  ),
  annotate(
    "text", x = c(20, 73), y = -59, label = c("← Worse health", "Better health →"), hjust = c(0, 1),
    size = g24_text, colour = g24l_note
  )
)

g24l_vitality_frame <- list(
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = g24l_rule),
  scale_size_area(max_size = 6.6, guide = "none"),
  g24l_y_title("Change in Republican margin over Democrats, 2012-16, % points"),
  g24_value_axis(breaks = seq(-50, 50, 25)),
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(20, 70, 10)),
  g24l_direction_labels,
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(20, 73), ylim = c(-50.5, 50), expand = FALSE, clip = "off"),
  g24_theme(),
  g24l_scatter_theme(),
  theme(axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(t = g24_size * 1.6)))
)
g24l_vitality_caption <- paste0(
  "*Weighted index of obesity, diabetes, heavy drinking, physical exercise and\nlife expectancy, 2010-12\n",
  "Sources: Atlas of US Presidential Elections; Census Bureau;\n",
  "IPUMS, University of Minnesota; Institute for Health Metrics\n",
  "and Evaluation; The Economist"
)
```

```{r g24-lines-vitality-highlight, econ_size = "two_column", econ_height = 275}
## The two labelled counties, in Ohio: each has a leader line from its label down to its dot.
g24l_called_out <- data.frame(
  label = c("Jefferson, OH", "Knox, OH"), health = c(32.2, 46), swing = c(30.3, 13),

)

g24l_vitality_hl <- ggplot(g24l_counties_hl, aes(health, swing)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = focus, size = pop), alpha = g24l_bubble_alpha, stroke = 0) +
```
